title: CHAPTER NINE. On the infinity of God; extensive and intensive
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER NINE. Concerning ye infinity belonging toward God. And these things concerning ye first attribute belonging toward God, namely absolute necessity belonging toward existing: ye second follows, namely I. Infinity, which here ye highest perfection belonging toward ye divine essence, every term plus limit lacking, is. Ye vocabulary belonging toward INFINITY here from those things which otherwise properly unto quantity are attributed we borrow. But God in two ways a term belonging toward His perfection to lack is said, namely extensively plus intensively. Extensively, because His nature precisely unto one genus belonging toward perfections limited is not, but in itself all genera belonging toward perfections whatever thought or in any way be can encloses, plus that infinitely. And so God simply plus absolutely perfect is called, because every perfection so necessarily in Him inheres that none at all unto Him can be lacking.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER NINE. On the infinity of God.

And these things concerning the first attribute of God, namely absolute necessity of existing: there follows the second, namely I. Infinity, which here is the highest perfection of the divine essence, lacking every term and limit. The vocabulary of INFINITY we here borrow from those things which otherwise are properly attributed to quantity.

But God is said in two ways to lack a term of His perfection, namely extensively and intensively. Extensively, because His nature is not precisely limited to one genus of perfections, but in itself encloses all genera of perfections whatever can be thought or be in any way, and that infinitely. And so God is called simply and absolutely perfect, because every perfection so necessarily inheres in Him that none at all can be lacking to Him.
source_text: CAPUT NONUM, De infinitate Dei. Atque haec de primo Dei attributo, nempe absoluta exsistendi necessitate: sequitur alterum, nimirum I. Infinitas, quae hic est, summa essentiae divinae perfectio, omni termino ac limite carens. INFINITATIS vocabulum hic mutuamur ab iis, quae quantitati alias proprie tribuuntur. Dicitur autem Deus duobus modis perfectionis suae termino carere, extensive videlicet & intensive. Extensive, quia ejus natura non est praecise limitata ad unum genus perfectionum, sed in se concludit omnia perfectionum genera, quaecunque cogitari aut esse ullo modo possunt, idque in infinitum. Atque ita Deus simpliciter & absolute perfectus dicitur, quia omnis perfectio illi ita necessario inest, ut nulla prorsus illi deesse queat.
